summary_paragraph: The patient was admitted with progressive fatigue and shortness of breath over four days, initially evaluated for possible stent restenosis or pulmonary embolism. He had no chest pain but reported dyspnea at rest improved with sublingual nitroglycerin. CT angiography showed resolution of prior pulmonary emboli with no new clots, and cardiac catheterization revealed no in-stent restenosis or new coronary lesions. His symptoms were attributed to chronic stable angina, and he was started on isosorbide mononitrate for symptom control. Anticoagulation was transitioned from heparin back to warfarin with bridging Lovenox. The patient remained stable, euvolemic, and without arrhythmias. He was discharged home with updated medications and follow-up plans.
problems: Coronary atherosclerosis of native coronary artery
Personal history of venous thrombosis and embolism
